newsitem.title: ITALY: WFP sees possible breakthrough in refugee exodus.
newsitem.headline: WFP sees possible breakthrough in refugee exodus.

text.p: The U.N.'s food aid agency on Friday welcomed evidence that Rwandan Hutus fleeing fighting in east Zaire's Goma region were crossing into Rwanda and said it had enough relief in place to feed 200,000 of them for 10 days.

"This is the break we've been hoping for. While it may not effect all the (refugee) population in terms of everybody coming back it could be a major breakthrough if they cross into Rwanda," said World Food Programme spokesman Trevor Rowe.
Rowe told Reuters the WFP had pre-positioned 750 tonnes of food at Gisenyi, Rwanda's northwestern border crossing with Zaire, after fighting erupted in eastern Zaire last month.

"It's enough to feed 200,000 people for 10 days. We also have an additional 300,000 rations pre-positioned on the Tanzania-Uganda border, which can be delivered within 48 hours to any additional refugee surge, should it develop," Rowe said.
The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said in Geneva that at least 10,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees had crossed into Rwanda and that some 100,000 more were heading for the border.
The refugees fled into Zaire after the Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis in 1994 and many fear reprisals back home for their role in the slaughter.
